quiet-hours.title: Quiet time in Microsoft Teams for mobile devices – Microsoft Support
quiet-hours.notes: Quiet time is a scheduled setting that silences Teams notifications on mobile devices so people can focus or disconnect while away. Users turn it on in the Teams app under the notification settings by enabling the option to block notifications during quiet hours. They can choose particular hours of the day, whole days of the week, or both. A further option applies the same schedule to the Teams and Outlook mobile apps tied to the same Microsoft account, and the schedule is also passed to Viva Insights for weekly and monthly summaries. While quiet time is active, no sounds or push notifications appear, but new messages and activity remain visible once the app is opened. Other people cannot tell that notifications are muted, so the page suggests a status message as an alternative signal. The times follow the device clock and adjust automatically when the time zone changes. The page covers mobile devices only and does not mention desktop clients or any licence requirement.

react-pattern.title: Agent Factory: The new era of agentic AI – common use cases and design patterns – Microsoft Azure Blog
react-pattern.notes: The Azure blog presents ReAct, short for reason plus act, as one of several agentic design patterns. In this pattern an agent alternates between thinking and doing: it carries out a step, observes the outcome, and then decides what to do next. The goal is to solve problems as they unfold, especially where a fixed plan is not enough because of ambiguity, changing requirements, or an unclear best path. Each new observation feeds the next decision, so the agent can adapt its approach on the fly. The blog illustrates this with an enterprise IT support agent that diagnoses an issue by asking follow-up questions, checking system logs, trying possible fixes, and adjusting its strategy. When a case becomes too complex or falls outside its scope, the agent hands it to a human specialist together with a detailed summary. The post positions ReAct as a building block that can be combined with tool use, reflection, planning, and multi-agent patterns. It gives no formal definition and does not list technical drawbacks.

reranking.title: Semantic ranking overview – Azure AI Search – Microsoft Learn
reranking.notes: Azure AI Search offers a semantic ranker, a set of query-side capabilities that re-scores an initial result list produced by keyword or reciprocal-rank-fusion ranking. It works on text queries, the text part of vector queries, and hybrid queries, and relies on multilingual deep-learning models adapted from Bing. Only a limited set of top results is passed to the second stage, and for each document selected fields from a semantic configuration, such as title, keywords, and content, are combined into one summary string that is truncated if too long. The ranker assigns a new relevance score on a fixed scale where higher means a better answer to the query. It can also return captions with highlights and, optionally, a direct answer, both taken verbatim from the indexed content. Query rewriting is available in preview. The feature suits prose-heavy content such as knowledge bases and documentation. It is a billed premium feature offered in selected regions, with a free monthly allowance. Its limits are that it reorders only the existing result set and generates no new text.

restricted-sharepoint-search.title: Restricted SharePoint Search – SharePoint in Microsoft 365 – Microsoft Learn
restricted-sharepoint-search.notes: Restricted SharePoint Search lets administrators maintain an allow list of SharePoint sites that organisation-wide search, and temporarily Copilot Chat and agent experiences, may draw from. It is off by default with an empty list. The page presents it as a temporary measure that gives admins time to review permissions before content is overshared, not as a security boundary, and it does not change site permissions. Admins manage it with PowerShell cmdlets for enabling, disabling, and curating the list, and changes take effect within about an hour. Answers can still draw on content the user can already reach, such as their own OneDrive files, chats, mail, calendar, and recently used or directly shared files. The allow list is capped, a hub site counts as a single entry, and there is no deny list, so it cannot block individual sites. Copilot may give less complete answers while it is on. The page recommends cleaning up permissions with SharePoint Advanced Management and Microsoft Purview, and notes the feature is being phased out in favour of Restricted Content Discovery.

sap-s4hana.title: SAP S/4HANA in Linux on Azure – Azure Architecture Center – Microsoft Learn
sap-s4hana.notes: This Azure Architecture Center guide describes how to run SAP S/4HANA, and Suite on HANA, on Linux in Azure with high availability and disaster recovery. It does not define S/4HANA itself but shows a typical production layout. The application layer consists of Fiori front-end servers, SAP Web Dispatcher, application servers, and a Central Services cluster. The database layer uses SAP HANA on clustered Linux virtual machines with HANA System Replication and automatic failover. Central Services contain single points of failure, so they need highly available NFS storage and fencing. Fiori can also be embedded directly in the S/4 system, which removes the extra front-end VMs. Networking follows a hub-and-spoke design with separate subnets per tier, load balancers, and network security groups. HANA must run on VM types certified by SAP, and production storage must be premium-class disks rather than standard disks. Required SAP licences are the customer's responsibility. The guide notes limits such as unsuitability of Spot VMs for production and the need for cross-region disaster recovery to survive a regional outage.

sharepoint-2013-workflows.title: SharePoint 2013 workflow retirement – Microsoft Support
sharepoint-2013-workflows.notes: A workflow in SharePoint automates the movement of documents or list items through the steps of a business process, and organisations used it to attach business logic to lists and libraries. SharePoint 2013 workflows were typically built and published with SharePoint Designer 2013, while developers used Visual Studio. Microsoft is retiring them in SharePoint Online in stages: the older 2010 workflows ended first, 2013 workflows were switched off for new tenants, and removal from existing tenants, including government clouds, follows on the date given on the page. Admins can block creation of new 2013 workflows with a PowerShell tenant setting. Existing workflows keep running and stay editable until the shutdown, after which they can only be viewed as raw XML files. On-premises SharePoint Server versions keep supporting them until their own end of support. The recommended replacements are Power Automate, the built-in approvals feature, and partner solutions, and the Microsoft 365 Assessment tool helps find where workflows are in use.

sharepoint-designer.title: Introducing SharePoint Designer – Microsoft Support
sharepoint-designer.notes: SharePoint Designer 2013 is a locally installed web and application design program for creating and customising SharePoint sites and applications, and the page says this can be done without writing code. With it, users build data-driven pages, workflow-based solutions, and site designs, and can package a finished solution as a template. It connects to lists and libraries as well as external data such as SQL Server, OLE DB, SOAP and REST services, XML files, and external content types through Business Connectivity Services. Views, forms, web parts, and navigation can be designed, and workflows are assembled from events, conditions, actions, and steps, with an import path from Visio. Master pages, page layouts, and CSS files support branding, though by default only site collection administrators may edit them. Administrators can restrict features through a settings page. It targets SharePoint 2013 and later sites. The page states that support for SharePoint Designer 2013 is scheduled to end in July 2026, and some data options are not available in every SharePoint deployment.

soap.title: SOAP, REST, and More – MSDN Magazine (archive) – Microsoft Learn
soap.notes: This archived MSDN Magazine column compares SOAP with REST. It describes SOAP as a protocol specification for exchanging data between two endpoints, whereas REST is an architectural style. SOAP was created to give different platforms and languages an interoperable way to communicate, and it is deliberately not tied to HTTP so it can run over other transports. WSDL metadata allows client proxies to be generated, and the WS-* extensions add features such as message-level security across protocols, federated identity, and atomic distributed transactions. The author lists drawbacks: SOAP over HTTP POST cannot use HTTP caching, services are harder to scale, vendor differences in the many standards complicate interoperability, and distributed transactions raise coupling. The claim that SOAP is more secure than REST is rejected, since both usually rely on HTTP authentication with TLS. The column concludes that SOAP is worth choosing when a specific SOAP feature is needed, and that otherwise REST usually offers better characteristics. The page is a 2009 opinion piece rather than a formal specification.

solution-publisher.title: Solution concepts – Power Platform – Microsoft Learn
solution-publisher.notes: In Power Platform every app and other component belongs to a solution, and every solution has a publisher that is chosen when the solution is created. The publisher indicates who developed the app and acts as the owner of components created in its solutions. The owner decides which changes other publishers may make to those components, and ownership can move within one publisher but not across publishers. Each publisher carries a prefix, such as a short company name, which is added to the names of the metadata it creates and helps avoid naming collisions when solutions from different publishers are installed in the same environment. Because metadata names cannot be renamed after creation, the prefix should be set before any apps or metadata are built. Without a custom solution, work lands in the default system solutions. The page advises creating a dedicated publisher with a meaningful name instead of using the default, and using a single publisher so the layering model can be changed later. Once a publisher is set on a component in a managed solution, it cannot be changed.

spatial-audio.title: Spatial audio in Microsoft Teams meetings – Microsoft Support
spatial-audio.notes: Spatial audio is an immersive audio option for Teams voice and video meetings in which each participant's voice seems to come from their relative position on the meeting screen. This lets listeners associate a voice with a person in the gallery view. It is switched on with a toggle in the audio settings, either before a meeting through the device settings or during a meeting through the more-actions menu, and the choice applies to future meetings. It needs wired USB stereo headphones or speakers, or a device's built-in stereo speakers, and Bluetooth audio devices are not supported at present. The gallery must show more than two participants. Teams turns the feature off automatically when network bandwidth or memory runs short. One-to-one calls and very large meetings are listed as not yet supported. With live interpretation, the original and translated audio play at the same volume unless the feature is turned off and the meeting rejoined, and music mode does not deliver high-fidelity audio while it is on. The page names no licence requirement.

stable-diffusion.title: Introducing Stability AI Generative Visual Models to Azure AI Foundry – Microsoft Tech Community
stable-diffusion.notes: This Microsoft announcement introduces Stability AI image models in Azure AI Foundry. Stable Diffusion 3.5 Large, a model with several billion parameters, is described as the most capable member of the Stable Diffusion family, and Stable Image Ultra builds on it while Stable Image Core builds on an improved SDXL. The models generate images from text at roughly one megapixel and also support image-to-image generation, which transforms an input picture while keeping its basic structure, for example for style transfer or restoration. The post lists uses in advertising, media, gaming, education, e-commerce, and publishing. Customers need an Azure AI Foundry project and deploy the models from the model catalog with managed compute, then call them through an API endpoint or the playground. Limits stated are that the models are not trained to depict real people or historical events factually, so they suit creative rather than authenticity-critical work, and Azure AI Content Safety is on by default and cannot be turned off. Performance claims come from the vendor.

subnetting.title: TCP/IP addressing and subnetting – Windows Client – Microsoft Learn
subnetting.notes: Subnetting means dividing a class A, B, or C network into smaller networks so that one block of IP addresses can serve several physical networks instead of requiring a separate block for each. A subnet mask is a 32-bit value whose ones mark the network portion of an address and whose zeros mark the host portion. The network ID has all zeros in the host part, while the broadcast address has all ones, so neither can be given to an individual host. A host compares a destination against its own mask to decide whether the target is local or must be sent to the default gateway. The page works through an example in which a single network is split into four equal subnets by choosing a longer mask, giving each of three sites its own range. All computers on one physical network must use addresses from the same subnet, and a wrongly configured mask breaks connections to neighbouring networks while distant ones may still work. The article covers only 32-bit IPv4 addressing.

teams-templates.title: Get started with team templates in the Teams admin center – Microsoft Teams – Microsoft Learn
teams-templates.notes: A team template defines the structure of a team for a particular business need or project, so administrators can roll out consistent teams and users can start collaboration spaces with predefined settings, channels, and apps. Templates are managed in the Teams admin center or with PowerShell, and custom ones can be created from scratch, from an existing team, or from another template. Template policies control which templates appear for which users and groups. A template can hold the type, name, description, visibility, team settings, channels, tabs, and apps, but not members, the team picture, files, connectors, or private and shared channels. Microsoft supplies prebuilt industry templates that can be duplicated but not edited, and some of them are connected templates that add SharePoint pages and lists as tabs. Each template has size limits on channels, tabs per channel, and apps, and more can be added after creation. Developers can also create teams from templates through Microsoft Graph. Sensitivity labels are not supported in GCC environments.

terraform-state.title: Store Terraform state in Azure Storage – Microsoft Learn
terraform-state.notes: Terraform state is the data Terraform uses to match deployed resources with the configuration, which tells it which Azure resources to add, update, or delete. By default the state is stored locally, which the page says is poor for teams, may expose sensitive information because the file can contain secrets in plain text, and raises the risk of accidental deletion. The recommended pattern is to keep it remotely in an Azure Storage blob container through the azurerm backend, configured with the storage account name, container name, and a key that names the state file. The access key is best supplied through an environment variable instead of being written to disk, and can also be stored in Key Vault. Blob storage locks the state automatically before write operations, preventing concurrent changes that could corrupt it, and data is encrypted at rest. The example uses an access key and open network access, which the page marks as unsuitable for production, where firewalls, service endpoints, or private endpoints and the most secure supported authentication should be used.

threat-explorer.title: Threat Explorer and real-time detections – Microsoft Defender for Office 365 – Microsoft Learn
threat-explorer.notes: Threat Explorer is a near real-time reporting tool in Microsoft Defender for Office 365 that helps security operations teams investigate and respond to threats. It is included in Plan 2, while the lighter real-time detections report is available in Plan 1. Threat Explorer offers more views, more filtering including saved queries, and more actions than the real-time report. Its views cover all email, malware, phish, campaigns, content malware, and URL clicks. Analysts filter by date range, message, file, and threat properties, and charts can be pivoted by values such as delivery action, sender domain, and detection technology. Data can be exported as CSV, and actions let admins remediate selected messages, preview or download an email, or move into hunting. Access needs a Defender for Office 365 licence and suitable permissions through Defender XDR roles, email and collaboration roles, or Entra roles, with least privilege advised. Real-time detections show only the state at delivery, whereas Threat Explorer also shows post-delivery activity. Preview and download work only while the message still exists in a cloud mailbox or quarantine.

unified-customer-profile.title: Unify customer data – Dynamics 365 Customer Insights - Data – Microsoft Learn
unified-customer-profile.notes: In Dynamics 365 Customer Insights, unification combines several customer data sources into a single customer profile record per customer, removing duplicates and merging key fields to break down data silos. It requires that data sources are already set up, and the page advises reviewing ingested data and filtering out unwanted rows first. The process has four steps. First, the customer data step selects source tables holding profile details such as name, phone, and address, but not one-to-many data like purchases, and maps columns to descriptive types. Second, deduplication rules find several rows for one customer and keep the best one. Third, matching conditions link records across tables into one consolidated record. Fourth, the unified data view lets admins decide which columns to include, exclude, or merge, for example combining several email columns into one. Each profile receives a CustomerId that stays stable between runs, except when profiles merge or split after changes to sources or rules, in which case a previous-ID field tracks the old values. The result feeds relationships, enrichment, activities, and measures.
